subject: Physics
b6_reason: A is true (extension of a helical spring comes from torsion/shear of its wire, so shear modulus governs it) while R is false (steel has far greater tensile strength than copper).
b6_working: Stretching a coil spring twists the wire, so the restoring behaviour depends on the shear (rigidity) modulus, not Young's modulus: A true. Tensile strength of steel is much higher than that of copper, so a copper coil spring is weaker, not stronger: R false. Hence 'A is true but R is false'.
